title: The Long Vector
premise: Mirabel Nystrom smuggles memories—recorded experiences pressed into black-market wafers—along the silent trade route between Earth and the quarantined colony of Vesper Reach, where an official massacre never happened. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical scenes of a purge that archives insist never occurred, Mirabel realizes the contraband wafer she's carried for years holds the only unaltered record of the event, planted in her by a dying courier who was more family than client. Hunted by customs enforcers and the corporation that rewrote history, she rallies the smugglers, dockworkers, and dream-children who've become her accidental family to broadcast the memory colony-wide before the reactor countdown—rigged as evidence destruction—reaches zero. The truth goes out; the quarantine breaks; and Mirabel, who spent her life invisible, finally belongs somewhere permanent.
about_author: Isandro Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that had lost diplomatic contact. They write about people who carry other people's truths across distances no one else will cross.

chapters.title: Cold Cargo
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She runs a memory-wafer shipment through Vesper Reach orbital customs using a dead man's transponder codes, establishing her solitary craft and the silent war between Earth and the colonies. Emotional beat: competent loneliness—the thrill of the run shadowed by the fact that no one would notice if she didn't come back.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Alike
chapters.summary: Dockworker Sefa's POV. Her daughter Anouk wakes screaming with a dream shared by forty colony children: fire, a sealed dome, names being struck from lists. Sefa brings the dream to Mirabel because smugglers hear things officials don't. Emotional beat: unease turning to dread as the dreams prove too detailed to be coincidence.

chapters.title: Wafer 77
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She examines the old wafer her dying courier mentor, Ovid, pressed into her hands years ago with the words 'when they start dreaming.' It's encrypted in his personal cipher. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing—she realizes Ovid knew this day would come and chose her to carry it.

chapters.title: Customs House Ghosts
chapters.summary: Enforcer Dae-Ho's POV, a customs officer who begins noticing anomalies: purged records, a gap in the colony census twenty years wide, and Mirabel's ship flagged in files that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: institutional loyalty cracking as he glimpses how deep the erasure goes.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Reactor technician Brey's POV. She discovers the plant's maintenance logs were rewritten and a countdown sequence installed—officially a 'decommissioning protocol,' unofficially set to slag every physical archive on the surface. Emotional beat: quiet horror of a careful person realizing the numbers don't add up.

chapters.title: Ovid's Cipher
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Using Ovid's letters and a lullaby he taught her, she cracks the first layer of Wafer 77: coordinates, dates, and a partial recording of the Amaranth Dome purge—people being loaded into shuttles that officially never launched. Emotional beat: vertigo of holding proof everyone says is impossible.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Circle
chapters.summary: Anouk's POV, age eleven. The children compare dreams and realize each child remembers a different name from the struck list—as if the massacre itself is trying to reassemble through them. Emotional beat: eerie wonder hardening into resolve; the children decide to find Mirabel themselves.

chapters.title: Invisible Routes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She seeks out the old smuggling network—retired pilots, a nun who launders data, a blind archivist—to authenticate the wafer. Most refuse out of fear; two join her. Emotional beat: the first fragile stitching of found family, strangers choosing risk over safety together.

chapters.title: Dae-Ho Closes In
chapters.summary: Dae-Ho's POV. He traces the wafer's provenance to Ovid and finds Ovid's death certificate filed three days after the man actually died—someone is still editing the past. He confronts Mirabel off the record. Emotional beat: wary alliance between hunter and hunted, neither trusting but both needing.

chapters.title: Countdown Made Public
chapters.summary: Brey's POV. The reactor countdown goes live on public displays, sold as routine decommissioning. Brey leaks the true timeline to Mirabel: eleven days until every archive melts. Emotional beat: urgency replacing caution—the clock is now a character.

chapters.title: The Name Anouk Carries
chapters.summary: Anouk's POV. The girl realizes the name in her dream—'Mirela Nystrom'—is Mirabel's mother, listed among the disappeared. Mirabel's family wasn't just from Vesper Reach; they were erased by it. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes Mirabel's exile as inheritance—she was always part of this story.

chapters.title: Earth Sends a Listener
chapters.summary: New POV: Auditor Ilse Varga arrives from Earth to certify the decommissioning, genuinely believing the official record. She interviews the dreaming children and is shaken when one describes her own brother—a man Earth also lost track of. Emotional beat: the antagonist's certainty beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Nun's
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The network is raided; the archivist is taken, and the safehouse burned. Someone sold them out—one of the two who joined her. Emotional beat: betrayal's sting, then the harder choice to trust the remaining family anyway, because invisibility failed them all.

chapters.title: The Second Layer
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Deciphering deeper into Wafer 77 reveals not just the massacre but its mechanism: a corporate memory-edit broadcast that overwrote the entire colony's recollection overnight. The children's dreams are the edit decaying. Emotional beat: terrible clarity—the enemy isn't hiding the past, it's actively deleting it, and time is on the enemy's side.

chapters.title: Ilse Descends
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She descends to the surface against orders and walks the sealed Amaranth Dome, finding physical residue the edits missed: scorch patterns, a child's shoe, unlogged shuttle fuel. Emotional beat: conversion—she stops auditing the record and starts testifying against it.

chapters.title: The Trap at Relay Nine
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A fake offer of broadcast access lures them to a relay station; it's an ambush. Dae-Ho, now openly defected, takes a bullet meant for Mirabel. Emotional beat: sacrifice and fury—the cost of belonging made flesh; they escape with the wafer intact but the network broken.

chapters.title: Forty Names
chapters.summary: Anouk's POV. The children pool their fragments and reconstruct the full list of the disappeared—all forty names, including Mirela Nystrom. They plan to read the names aloud on the colony's open band while the wafer broadcasts. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into ceremony; grief given structure and voice.

chapters.title: Two Days to Zero
chapters.summary: Brey's POV. Brey works to stall the countdown while Mirabel's remnant crew seizes the main broadcast spire. Ilse provides certification codes under her own name, knowing it ends her career. Emotional beat: converging resolve—every thread of the found family committing fully, no exits planned.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. Under fire on the spire, she plays Wafer 77 colony-wide: the purge, the shuttles, the forty names read by forty children. The memory-edit shatters as thousands remember at once. Emotional beat: catharsis—the invisible past erupting into light, and Mirabel finally seen.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Brey and Dae-Ho's alternating POV. With the truth public, the reactor crew refuses the final command; Brey kills the countdown manually as enforcers stand down rather than fire on a crowd that now remembers everything. Emotional beat: the machine stopped not by heroics alone but by ordinary people refusing, together.

chapters.title: Quarantine Broken
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Earth's blockade collapses under scandal; ships arrive carrying families of the disappeared. Ilse, stripped of rank, chooses to stay. Emotional beat: restitution without erasure—the dead honored, the living reunited, justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Long Vector Home
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, resolution. She could run any route in the system now; instead she stays, opening a school for memory-craft with Anouk as her first student, Ovid's wafer enshrined in the rebuilt dome. Emotional beat: belonging earned—she was never a vector between worlds, but the point where they finally meet.
